chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz and Fuzayl and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'For what reason is the twig placed with the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The punishment is averted from him as long as it is wet.'

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: The twig or fresh branch placed with the deceased
key_terms.رَطْبَةً: Fresh/moist (referring to the state of the twig)

ai.seo_question: Why is a twig placed with the deceased in Shia burial traditions?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical benefit of placing a fresh twig (jarida) with the deceased, explaining that its moisture acts as a shield against the punishment of the grave. This practice highlights the Shia belief in the tangible connection between physical elements and the spiritual state of the soul during the intermediate realm (Barzakh). The freshness of the twig symbolizes vitality, which temporarily mitigates the harshness of the grave's trials until the twig dries out.
